## Root-cause analysis (rebar-debug, re-verified on post-2421 origin/main @ c63d3d9)

**Proven root cause.** In `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, the mcp blue-green block's step-5b
store-readiness gate calls `record_backoff_failure` on a storeless-container refusal
(`mcp-store-missing`). That recorder writes the REVIEW-BOT `$BACKOFF_FILE`
(`$STATE_DIR/deploy-backoff`) and emits `deploy_failed`. `$BACKOFF_FILE` gates the WHOLE script
at the top, so a storeless mcp container would suppress the *review-bot* deploy — a component
that never ran on that tick. The separation is documented explicitly at `autodeploy.sh:64-69`
("writing it from the mcp path would let an mcp failure suppress the REVIEW-BOT deploy"), and
`MCP_BACKOFF_FILE` exists precisely to keep the two independent.

**Post-2421 shape.** Change 2421 (ticket 6ada) refactored the mcp recorders: `schedule_mcp_backoff`
(bookkeeping), `record_mcp_routine_backoff` (retire-cap/mem-abort, no page), and
`record_mcp_backoff_failure` (genuine failures, still pages via `err deploy_failed`). A
storeless-container refusal is a **genuine mcp failure** — the direct analog is the 5c
handshake gate, which already uses `record_mcp_backoff_failure` and documents the same
`NOT $BACKOFF_FILE` reasoning (autodeploy.sh:985-986). So the correct recorder is
`record_mcp_backoff_failure` (writes `mcp-deploy-backoff`/`MCP_BACKOFF_FILE`, pages, leaves the
review-bot `deploy-backoff` ABSENT).

**Proof (discriminating experiment).** New test on the `mcp_box` harness
(`test_storeless_refusal_backs_off_mcp_not_the_review_bot`): a healthy-but-storeless container
(`store.expected=true, present=false`) is refused (`mcp-store-missing` fires — precondition),
then asserts the observable backoff files. RED on current main: `mcp-deploy-backoff` absent and
`deploy-backoff` written (journal shows the `deploy_failed` marker) — the wrong component
throttled. GREEN after swapping to `record_mcp_backoff_failure`. Mutation check (re-seed the
exact `record_backoff_failure` defect, run in a macOS `sandbox-exec`) returns the test to RED —
the test has teeth.

**Defect legitimacy: `defect`.** Violates the cited design invariant at `autodeploy.sh:64-69`
and the AC. Standing intent documented → a fix, not a design escalation.

**Fix.** One line at the 5b branch: `record_backoff_failure` → `record_mcp_backoff_failure`
(+ an explanatory comment mirroring the 5c gate).

**Step-7 parity census (Axis 2).** Rule: "an mcp-path failure must record the mcp-scoped backoff
(`MCP_BACKOFF_FILE`), never the script-gating review-bot `$BACKOFF_FILE`." Census of the mcp
block's failure/deferral branches: mcp-checkout, mcp-rsync, mcp-secrets, mcp-build, mcp-tag,
mcp-run, mcp-unhealthy, **mcp-store-missing (5b — was the sole leak, now fixed)**,
mcp-handshake, mcp-flip all record `record_mcp_backoff_failure`; retire-cap / mem-abort use
`record_mcp_routine_backoff`. The five remaining `record_backoff_failure` call sites
(autodeploy.sh:793,796,812,823,833) are all inside `deploy_review_bot()` (lines 734-846), the
correct path. 5b was the only mcp-block branch writing the review-bot file — this is the
store-missing path 6ada's agent flagged as this same class, now covered. No other MISSING slots.

**Defect origin (`caused_by`).** Introducing commit `53fd464ba091` ("feat(mcp): report store
reachability from /health"), which added the entire 5b block including the wrong
`record_backoff_failure; exit 1` line (confirmed in its diff and by `git log -S mcp-store-missing`).
`git blame -w -M -C` attributes the recorder line to a July bot-path commit, but that is a
copy-detection **carrier** artifact — the text is identical to the bot-path recorder calls;
the block itself is new in `53fd464`. Ticket: **d9ab-7b5e-fe4c-4ff4** (the store-readiness gate
work). Close class `plan_defect`: the plan wired the review-bot recorder into an mcp-path gate.
